Bars show the predicted next-day return, centred on zero. ✓ means the predicted direction was right. Model forecasts are a few basis points (1 bp = 0.01%) because daily returns are mostly noise.

Scoreboard so far

Strategy: hold the stock tomorrow if the model forecasts a positive return, otherwise hold cash. Costs of 5 bp are charged on every switch. Everything is computed live, from the first test day up to the selected date, using the saved out-of-sample forecasts.

SPY, test period: what the tutorial LSTM predicted

Prove the lag: slide the LSTM's prediction earlier in time

If the model really forecast tomorrow, its day-to-day moves would line up with the market's on the same day. Slide its line back by a few days: the chart above moves with it. At 1 day earlier the orange line turns when the price turns, just smoother: it is following the past, not anticipating the future.

Volatility forecast vs what happened

Does the 99% risk limit hold?

Value-at-Risk (VaR) is the loss you expect to exceed on only 1% of days. Both lines below use the same HAR-RV + VIX volatility forecast. One assumes normal tails; the other uses the empirical tails of past returns (filtered historical simulation).
